name: Flambaum 2007 review: (R1) M_p ~ 3 Lambda_QCD -> the tree's H2, f = d ln m_p/d ln v = S; (R2) eq. (9) Th-229 nuclear-clock enhancement 1e5 (2 da/a + 0.5 dX_q/X_q - 5 dX_s/X_s)(7 eV/w)

source.located: V.V. Flambaum, 'Variation of fundamental constants: theory and observations', arXiv:0705.3704v2 [physics.atom-ph], 21 Jun 2007 (8 pp.). R1 at p.4 (sec. V, last paragraph before 'VI. Microwave clocks'); R2 at p.5 sec. VII, eq. (9); energy data p.5 refs [51]-[53]; eq. (9) attributed by the author to his Ref. [38] = Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 092502 (2006) = arXiv:physics/0604188 (not itself read here).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0705.3704 (all 8 pages returned verbatim, v2).

published_statement: R1 (p.4): 'The proton mass is proportional to Lambda_QCD (M_p ~ 3 Lambda_QCD), therefore, the measurements of the variation of the electron-to-proton mass ratio mu = m_e/M_p is equivalent to the measurements of the variation of X_e = m_e/Lambda_QCD.' R2 (p.5): 'As it is shown in Ref. [38] there is an additional very important advantage. The relative effects of variation of alpha and m_q/Lambda_QCD are enhanced by 5 orders of magnitude. A rough estimate for the relative variation of the 229Th transition frequency is dw/w ~ 10^5 (2 da/a + 0.5 dX_q/X_q - 5 dX_s/X_s) (7 eV/w) (9) where X_q = m_q/Lambda_QCD, X_s = m_s/Lambda_QCD, m_q = (m_u+m_d)/2 and m_s is the strange quark mass.' Energy context (p.5): 'A very narrow level (3.5+-1) eV above the ground state exists in 229Th nucleus [51] (in [52] the energy is (5.5+-1) eV, in [53] the energy is (7.6+-0.5) eV).'
published_hypotheses: R1-H1 chiral-limit proportionality: M_p ~ 3 Lambda_QCD with quark-mass contributions to M_p not written (used to set d mu/mu = d X_e/X_e exactly, p.4 and p.5 eq. 8 context)

R1-H2 only dimensionless ratios are measurable; X_e, X_q, X_s are defined in units of Lambda_QCD (p.4 'One can only measure the variation of dimensionless quantities'); Flambaum-Wiringa 0807.4943 p.1 makes the convention explicit: 'convenient to assume that Lambda_QCD is constant ... measure all masses and energies in units of Lambda_QCD'
R1-H3 no statement that Lambda_QCD is fixed while the Higgs vev varies; p.3-4 present GUT models where d Lambda/Lambda ~ 34 d alpha/alpha and dm/m ~ 70 d alpha/alpha ('model dependent')
R2-H1 'a rough estimate', taken from Ref. [38] (Flambaum PRL 97 092502, 2006); first-order linear response
R2-H2 the transition energy w is unknown in 2007: 3.5+-1, 5.5+-1 or 7.6+-0.5 eV; eq. (9) is normalised to 7 eV and scales as 1/w
R2-H3 X_q = m_q/Lambda_QCD with m_q = (m_u+m_d)/2 and X_s = m_s/Lambda_QCD treated as independent parameters
R2-H4 (implicit, from the alpha coefficient) a Coulomb-energy difference between isomer and ground state of 2e5 x 7 eV = 1.4 MeV
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (R1) address.py:446 labels Flambaum p.4 'this project's H2', and address.py:104 defines H2 as 'Lambda_QCD ITSELF FIXED: d ln m_p/d ln v = S'. Flambaum states a proportionality and a units convention (R1-H2); he does not state that Lambda_QCD is physically fixed while v varies, and his own sec. V models vary Lambda_QCD (R1-H3). 'Lambda fixed as v varies' is the tree's hypothesis carried on this citation; the tree names it and refuses H1-vs-H2 (address.py:331-334), so this is an attribution drift, not a hidden hypothesis.

ADDED (R1) address.py:505-509 / excite.py:164-165: the tree adds the Feynman-Hellmann light-quark fraction S (m_p = Lambda F(m_q/Lambda)); Flambaum's p.4 statement is the S -> 0 limit. Machine-checked here: with Lambda fixed, d ln m_p/d ln v = S exactly, and K_mu = S - 1 -> -1 reproduces Flambaum's mu == X_e identity at S = 0. A strict improvement on the source, not a weakening.

DROPPED-DATUM (R1) excite.py:164-165, 1542-1543 headline S = 0.06 = sigma_piN/m_p only; under H2 (Lambda_3 fixed, every quark mass proportional to v) the strange sigma term also enters S = sum_q sigma_q/m_p (address.py:505 docstring). The tree carries 0.09 'with strange sigma term' in S_SCAN (address.py:449-452), so the omission is in the headline figure, not in the scan.

WEAKENED-DATUM (R2) address.py:763, 776-785 evaluate eq. (9) at omega = TH229_OMEGA_EV = 7.0 eV, i.e. the (7 eV/w) factor set to 1; the transition is now measured at 8.355733554 eV, factor 0.8377. Not flagged in the tree (no occurrence of 8.35 / 2020407 / Beeks in address.py or excite.py).

ADDED (R2) address.py:281-282, 766-773: d ln X_q/d ln v = d ln X_s/d ln v (= 7/9 under H1, 1 under H2) because both quark masses go as v; Flambaum treats X_q and X_s as independent (R2-H3). Named in the tree ('both quark masses go as v'), a consequence of the tree's fixed-Yukawa premise. Under it the X_q and X_s terms partially cancel (0.5 - 5 = -4.5) and the X_s coefficient carries 91% of the magnitude.

ADDED (R2) address.py:776-785: K_alpha(H1) = 43 alpha/(54 pi) from the tree's own one-loop result inserted into Flambaum's alpha term; its share of the inner bracket is 1.06e-3 under H1, so the (now-contradicted) alpha coefficient does not move the tree's figure.

PRESERVED (R2) address.py:294-295, 760-764 carry the author's 'a rough estimate' as ORDER (TH229_IS_ORDER = True). But address.py:285-288 prints 'eps_det(Th-229 courier) = 2.9e-24 -- EIGHT ORDERS BETTER' and 2.86e-24 to three figures from an ORDER input; the digits exceed what the source supports (over-representation of precision, not of sign or order).

NOT FROM THIS SOURCE: the clock accuracy 1e-18 (address.py section 10 print, excite.py:44-47) is the tree's ORDER fixture; 0705.3704 gives no Th-229 clock accuracy. Beeks et al. 2407.17300 p.1 cite a projected 1e-19 for Th3+ and report spectroscopy 'at the 10^-12 precision level'.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. What Flambaum had in June 2007: the Th-229m energy only from gamma-ray differences (3.5+-1, 5.5+-1, 7.6+-0.5 eV); no measured isomer quadrupole moment or charge-radius difference; the alpha and strong coefficients from one rough model estimate (his 2006 PRL, Walecka-type reasoning); older sigma-term values (not used by his R1). What came later: (1) w = 8.355733554 eV laser-measured (2024); (2) Delta Q0/Q0 = 1.791(2)% and Delta<r^2> = 0.0105(13) fm^2, giving a measured-input K_alpha = 5900(2300) (2024/25), corroborated by microscopic theory K ~ 1e3-1e4 (2026) and halo/geometric modelling ~1e4 (2024); (3) sigma_piN 59.1(3.5) dispersive vs 43.7(3.6) lattice, sigma_s 28.6(9.3). Does it change the conclusion? EVIDENCE FOR M's hypothesis: the alpha coefficient of eq. (9) is ~28x (20-47x at 1 sigma) larger than what the new data imply -- the missing Q0/<r^2> data moved it by more than an order of magnitude; the (7 eV/w) factor moved by 16%. EVIDENCE AGAINST / LIMITING: the author labelled eq. (9) 'a rough estimate' and carried a factor-2.2 uncertainty in w, so this is the estimate being superseded by data, not an established result shown false; the X_q and X_s coefficients (which carry the tree's figure; X_s alone 91%) remain unmeasured, the published X_q estimates scatter over 3.75x in BOTH directions (Flambaum-Wiringa 2008 is 3.3x HIGHER than eq. 9), and no later computation of the X_s coefficient was found. R1 (M_p proportional to Lambda_QCD) is unmoved by any datum: dimensional transmutation makes it exact in the chiral limit, and the quark-mass correction is the S the tree already adds. For the tree: the moved data change eps_det(Th-229) by x1.19 (w) and plausibly up to ~x10 (enhancement ~1e4), and the H2 stable-matter density by x0.64-1.29 (S); none changes the order-of-magnitude verdicts they feed as far as computed here.
grade_evidence: Two results under one key. R1 (M_p ~ Lambda_QCD, the tree's H2 input): STANDS as the chiral-limit proportionality, with the tree's extension to f = S machine-checked exact (sympy) and the 'Lambda fixed' premise being the tree's own named hypothesis carried on Flambaum's citation (attribution drift address.py:446 / :104, not a hidden hypothesis); its datum S is contested (sigma_piN 43.7 vs 59.1 MeV; sigma_s 28.6) and moves the H2 density x0.64-1.29, not the verdict. R2 (eq. 9) -- the controlling part -- transcription exact and the tree's coefficients reproduced to 1e-12, but the conclusion moves with data that have moved: (i) w measured at 8.355733554 eV vs the 7 eV the tree evaluates at (address.py:763): coefficient x0.8377, eps_det 2.86e-24 -> 3.41e-24; (ii) eq. (9)'s alpha coefficient is 28x the measured-input K_alpha = 5900(2300) (Beeks 2024), corroborated by K ~ 1e3-1e4 (Minkov-Palffy 2026) and ~1e4 (Caputo 2024) -- this term carries only 1e-3 of the tree's figure; (iii) the X_q/X_s coefficients that carry the figure are unmeasured and contested (X_q estimates spread 3.75x; X_s never independently recomputed in what was read; a ~1e4 strong enhancement would raise eps_det 10x to 3.4e-23). Not WRONG: the author called eq. (9) 'a rough estimate', no counterexample to the strong-sector terms is shown, and the alpha discrepancy is an estimate superseded by data. Not STANDS: a datum the figure depends on has moved and the controlling coefficients are contested. The tree's own claim that section 9's verdict is independent of the value was NOT re-verified in this stage; the computed scenarios keep the nuclear courier > 1e3 better than the electronic one.
what_would_change_the_grade: Toward STANDS/NARROWED: the tree re-evaluating th229_coefficient at the measured w (8.355733554 eV) and demonstrating (by computation over an enhancement range ~1e3-1e6) that section 9's verdict is independent of the eq. (9) value -- the dependence would then be confined to a reported figure, grade NARROWED (eq. 9 holds only as an ORDER bound, alpha term superseded). Toward WRONG for the tree's use: a computed or measured X_q/X_s sensitivity of Th-229m below ~1e3 (the scale at which the courier stops beating the electronic one by >1e3), or a Th-229 vs optical-clock comparison under a known variation. For R1: none plausible -- only a different premise about what is held fixed as v varies (the tree's refused H1/H2 docket).
